correctness.rationale: Root the cyclic ordering at a designated sampled point (not the first point after a fixed origin); rotation then makes the other n-1 starts iid uniform on the interval, so the n gaps are Dirichlet, represented by iid mean-one exponentials divided by their sum T. This rooting leaves all claimed statistics unchanged. At u=log(n)+x and v=log(n)+log(log(n))+y the two marginal mean counts converge to exp(-x) and exp(-y). Integrating over the common exponential gives the mixed overlap (v-u+1)exp(-v) and the two-sum overlap 2exp(-v)-exp(-2v); n times each tends to zero. Disjoint supports are independent, and the finite-index Poisson process approximation therefore gives independent limiting type totals. T/n changes both thresholds by o_P(1); the probability of an exponential or gamma-two value in either resulting threshold band is bounded by the expected count in deterministic bands of width 2 epsilon plus the normalization error probability. The band term is O(epsilon) by the respective densities. Both zero counts give exactly the joint maxima event. For equal clockwise closed arcs the closest previous start dominates farther starts for coverage, so the largest-gap condition is exact. Removing one start merges its two adjacent gaps; taking the maximum over choices gives exactly the largest adjacent cyclic sum, including n=3.
residual_risks: The stored finite numerical claims are not used as a proof. The Dirichlet representation is used after rooting at a sample start; individual gap coordinates rooted at a fixed origin need not have the symmetric law.
